raw_case_text: A 38-year-old Liberian female with a 12-week gestation presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of low-grade subjective fever, night sweats, unintentional weight loss, gradually worsening abdominal pain, and intermittent spotting. Vital signs were stable on presentation, physical exam noticeable for gravida abdomen, otherwise unremarkable. Laboratory examination revealed beta hCG 118471, which was otherwise unremarkable. Pelvic ultrasound confirmed a 12-week viable intrauterine pregnancy. The patient was admitted to the hospital for close monitoring. Hospital course was complicated by massive pleural effusion, low-grade fever, progressive worsening abdominal pain, and spontaneous abortion. Non-contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the chest (Figure 1) revealed large right-sided pleural effusion, and contrast-enhanced computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis (Figure 2) revealed bilateral hilar adenopathy, ascites, thickening and enhancement of the peritoneum, and mottled nodular-appearing soft tissue consistent with omental caking suspicious for peritoneal carcinomatosis. She underwent extensive workup including surgical and oncologist consultations for possible exploratory laparotomy and discussion of treatment options for presumed ovarian neoplasm. Blood work revealed elevated carbohydrate antigen (CA) 125 and positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold, but adenosine deaminase, CA 19, alpha-fetoprotein, and inhibin B were within normal limits. Diagnostic laparoscopy with biopsy revealed significant pelvis ascites and diffuse miliary lesions throughout the peritoneum. She underwent dilatation and curettage; histopathologic examination showed chronic granulomatous inflammation with no evidence of neoplasm. Special stains on tissue sections and ascitic fluid stain revealed rare acid-fast bacilli, suggestive of mycobacterial granulomatous peritonitis. Additional questioning indicated a history of positive PPD skin test a year prior without follow-up treatment. The patient was placed on four-drug anti-tuberculous therapy and had a complete recovery.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 38-year-old pregnant female at 12 weeks of gestation presented with a 3-week history of low-grade fever, night sweats, unintentional weight loss, worsening abdominal pain, and intermittent vaginal spotting.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: A 38-year-old female (gravida at 12 weeks gestation) presented to the emergency department with a 3-week history of subjective low-grade fevers, night sweats, unintentional weight loss, gradually progressive abdominal pain, and intermittent vaginal spotting. During hospitalization, her course was complicated by worsening abdominal pain, development of a massive right-sided pleural effusion, and spontaneous abortion.
subjective.past_medical_history: Immigrant from Liberia. Gravida at 12 weeks gestation. Positive PPD skin test documented 1 year prior without subsequent preventive therapy. No other prior medical history, hospitalizations, or antibiotic exposures documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for low-grade fever, night sweats, unintentional weight loss, abdominal pain, and vaginal spotting. Negative for cough or dyspnea initially. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Hemodynamically stable. Gravid abdomen corresponding to 12 weeks gestation; physical examination otherwise unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Beta-hCG 118,471 mIU/mL. Pelvic ultrasound confirmed viable 12-week intrauterine pregnancy. Serum CA-125 elevated; QuantiFERON-TB Gold positive. Adenosine deaminase, CA 19-9, alpha-fetoprotein, and inhibin B within normal limits.
objective.advanced_workup: Non-contrast chest CT: large right-sided pleural effusion. Contrast-enhanced CT abdomen and pelvis: bilateral hilar adenopathy, ascites, peritoneal thickening and enhancement, and mottled nodular soft tissue consistent with omental caking, suspicious for peritoneal carcinomatosis. Dilatation and curettage performed post-miscarriage. Diagnostic laparoscopy with peritoneal biopsy: gross pelvic ascites, diffuse miliary peritoneal lesions, and histopathology showing chronic granulomatous inflammation without neoplasia.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Tuberculous peritonitis and pleuritis (disseminated abdominal tuberculosis) complicated by spontaneous abortion, mimicking advanced ovarian carcinomatosis, confirmed by positive QuantiFERON-TB Gold, laparoscopic peritoneal biopsy showing chronic granulomatous inflammation, and detection of rare acid-fast bacilli on tissue histological sections and ascitic fluid stain. Management & Outcome: Underwent dilatation and curettage following spontaneous abortion and initiated on 4-drug antituberculous therapy (rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, ethambutol). Achieved complete clinical and radiologic recovery.
